findings.title: Team admin/owner authorization uses AND instead of OR
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), so a team admin who is not also the team owner fails the check. Such users are rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they are separately the organizer or an attendee, even though the variable name and intended permission indicate admin OR owner should be sufficient.

findings.title: Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not de-duplicate the request itself
findings.body: uniqueGuests only removes guests that exactly match an existing attendee email and compares the raw guest string against a lower-cased blacklist. It does not lower-case guests or de-duplicate within the submitted array. A direct API call such as ['A@example.com', 'a@example.com'], or re-adding an existing attendee with different capitalization, can create duplicate attendee rows and duplicate invites, and a blacklisted address can bypass the blacklist by changing capitalization.

findings.title: Email sender receives the raw guest list instead of the filtered unique guest list
findings.body: The handler filters duplicates/blacklisted addresses into uniqueGuests for the database write, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered input. Existing attendees who were correctly filtered out of the write are therefore classified as new guests by sendAddGuestsEmails and receive a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail invitation instead of the guests-added notification.

findings.title: Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings
findings.body: The handler never checks booking.status or booking.endTime before creating attendees, updating the calendar, and sending guests-added/scheduled emails with a CONFIRMED ICS. A direct API caller can therefore mutate a cancelled, rejected, unconfirmed, or already-ended booking and cause new calendar/email invitations to be sent for an event that is not an accepted upcoming booking.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's
findings.body: The handler explicitly authorizes non-organizers (team admins/owners and attendees), but then loads credentials with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and constructs EventManager from the caller. The calendar event and destination calendar belong to booking.user/organizer, so for those authorized non-organizer callers EventManager cannot use the organizer's calendar credential and the external calendar attendee update can silently fail while the database and emails succeed, leaving systems inconsistent. The booking organizer's credentials/user should be used.

findings.title: Guest list has no maximum length
findings.body: The input schema accepts an arbitrarily large guests array. The handler then creates all attendees, loads a translation per attendee, updates the calendar, and sends email to the organizer/team plus every attendee. Any authorized caller, including an attendee, can use this for large-scale email fan-out/resource consumption and send platform-generated meeting invitations to many arbitrary addresses; the server should enforce a reasonable cap.

findings.title: Guests-added emails ignore disabled standard email settings
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees and takes no eventTypeMetadata argument. Unlike the other booking-change senders in this file, it does not check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType metadata. Event types configured to disable standard host/attendee emails will still send these emails.

findings.title: MultiEmail imports the @calcom/ui barrel from inside the same package
findings.body: MultiEmail lives in @calcom/ui but imports Button, EmailField, Icon, and Tooltip from the '@calcom/ui' barrel, while that barrel exports MultiEmailLazy which dynamically imports this file. This creates a self-referential import cycle and pulls the whole UI barrel into a component that was specifically made lazy, risking circular-chunk/undefined-import problems and defeating the intended code splitting. The component should import from relative component paths.

findings.title: Dialog state is not reset when closed without Cancel
findings.body: multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail are only cleared by the explicit Cancel button or on mutation success. Closing the dialog through the dialog close affordance, Escape, or overlay only calls setIsOpenDialog, so previously typed emails and a stale validation error remain the next time the dialog is opened and can be submitted accidentally. Editing the emails also does not clear isInvalidEmail after the user fixes the input.

findings.title: No tests cover the new addGuests mutation
findings.body: This PR adds a new mutation with organizer/team-admin/team-owner/attendee authorization branches, duplicate and blacklist filtering, database writes, calendar updates, and email fan-out, but adds no handler or integration tests. Tests should cover at least outsider rejection, admin versus owner access, organizer/attendee access, duplicate/blacklisted guests, and non-accepted bookings so authorization and filtering regressions are caught.
